question_text: A 73-year-old man is admitted to the hospital for jaundice and weight loss. He is an immigrant from the Dominican Republic and speaks little English. A CT scan is performed showing a large mass at the head of the pancreas. When you enter the room to discuss these results with the patient, his daughter and son ask to speak with you outside of the patient's room. They express their desire to keep these results from their father, who is "happy" and would prefer not to know his poor prognosis. What is the appropriate response in this situation?

Question: A 73-year-old man is admitted to the hospital for jaundice and weight loss. He is an immigrant from the Dominican Republic and speaks little English. A CT scan is performed showing a large mass at the head of the pancreas. When you enter the room to discuss these results with the patient, his daughter and son ask to speak with you outside of the patient's room. They express their desire to keep these results from their father, who is "happy" and would prefer not to know his poor prognosis. What is the appropriate response in this situation?

Options:
opa. Explore the reasoning behind the children's reluctance to have their father know his prognosis
opb. Tell the children that you are obligated to tell the father his prognosis
opc. Respect the children's wishes to hold prognosis information from their father
opd. Deliver the information in English so that you have not withheld information but the patient will not understand
ope. Bring the situation to the hospital ethics panel
